2.text: Wuˊthɪtčä-čaˊkêt-tɵˊmg̣ɪn (“middle sister-mate”) Middle sister (said by female).
2.note: Established this page's habit here: vowel between t and 'mgɪn is barred-o ɵ (U+0275, key gloss "between o and u, long"), and the g in -mgɪn carries dot-below (U+0323), confirmed at 4x. Applied consistently to every -tɵ'mg̣ɪn occurrence on the page rather than re-zooming each one.

3.text: Ñêˊnča-čaˊkêt-tɵˊmg̣ɪn (“younger sister-mate”). Younger sister (said by female).

4.note: The small raised loop after ê is read as laryngeal ᵋ (U+1D4B), not an uncatalogued superscript g — matches the shape and behaviour recorded in the reader's own memory note for this class (a stacked open-e outline that looks like a rounded loop with a tail at small scale). Recurs on L5, L6, L16.

5.text: Yêᵋˊlo Male cousin, paternal and maternal.

6.text: Ñaw-yêᵋˊlhɪ-tɵˊmg̣ɪn (in respect to male cousins)¹ Female cousin, paternal and maternal.
6.resolved: Ñ=N+U+0303; ê=e+U+0302; ᵋ=U+1D4B; ˊ=U+02CA (x2); ɪ=U+026A; ɵ=U+0275; g̣=g+U+0323; ¹=U+00B9 footnote marker

9.resolved: ᴇ=U+1D07 small-cap (x2); ʟ=U+029F small-cap (x2); ˊ=U+02CA (x2); ê=e+U+0302; g̣=g+U+0323
9.note: ᴇ/ʟ read as small-caps (distinct phonemes per §2.3/§2.5: obscure vowel ᴇ, lateral ʟ), not English capitalization — the word is Tier-1 vocabulary and there is no reading in which mid-word ASCII caps make sense here. Height in the 4x crop is consistent with this page's small-cap sort across every ᴇʟ- occurrence (L9-12, L20, L22, L25, L48).

13.text: Of all these terms, a collective may be formed by means of the word

14.text: -ret, -rat, which signifies “collection,” “set,” and is used only in combination

15.text: with others. Thus, yɪčemreˊt, “company of brothers;” čakêˊttɪrat, “company

16.text: of sisters” (in regard to the male relatives); yêᵋˊlhɪrat, “company of male

17.text: cousins;” kret, “company of boys” (k shortened for kmiˊñɪn, “boy,” “child”).
17.note: mz draft read the italic cross-reference letter as 'E' — raster shows lowercase italic k, matching "k shortened for kmi'ñɪn".

18.text: The fourth degree of relationship is designated by means of the stem

20.text: yɪlh-ᴇʟuˊê, “great-grandson;” yɪlhɪʟoˊo-tɵˊmg̣ɪn, “male cousin twice removed,” etc.

21.text: The more remote degrees of relationship are designated as čɪmčeˊkin,

22.text: “the near one;” or čičeˊtkin, čičeˊʟeñ, “kinsman.” The compass of the second

23.text: term is larger than that of the first.

24.text: All degrees of step-relations are designated with the suffix -lqäl, meaning

25.text: “intended for.”⁴ Thus ᴇʟɪˊhɪlqäl, “step-father;” ᴇʟaˊlqäl, step-mother,” also,
25.note: Printed exactly as read: "step-father;" closes with a curly close-quote, then ᴇʟa'lqäl, step-mother," carries only a closing quote with no matching open quote before "step-mother" — an asymmetric/unpaired quote in the print itself, not a keying choice. Kept as printed per §2.14 (printer's setting, not repaired).

26.text: in polygamous families, “another wife of my father;” eˊkkelqäl, “step-son;”

27.note: Advisory: rare form yiˊčemit-tuˊmgälqäl (keying_spec §5.1). Checked at 4x (review/3-005/zoom/zoom4-25p5-38_25p36-68.png neighbourhood and the lines-24-30 sheet): plain dotted i (not ɪ) in yiˊčemit, bare ä with no missing mark found.

28.text: “step-sister” (in repect to the brother), etc. Even ñew-miˊrg̣ɪlqäl, “step-grand-
28.note: "repect" for "respect" is the book's own printing error, keyed verbatim per §2.14 (printer's errors are keyed as printed).

29.text: mother,” is often used in polygamous families.

31.note: Run-in-heading-style small-caps setting keyed as plain ASCII capitals per §2.13.

34.note: A raised, dotted, italic-shaped small "i" sits above the final r of ulpEr in the raster (confirmed at 4x, review/3-005/zoom/zoom4-34p18-69.png) and is not part of the keyed text. It is not a footnote digit — the page's footnote markers are all superscript digits 1-6, fully accounted for elsewhere (opened at L42-47), and a letter shape is outside §2.10's marker inventory. It does not match any mark in §2.1-2.4. Left unkeyed per the uncatalogued-mark rule (§5.9/§2.14); flagging for adjudication rather than guessing at what it represents.

36.resolved: č=c+U+030C; ê=e+U+0302; ˊ=U+02CA (x2); ɪ=U+026A; ⁶=U+2076 footnote marker

37.note: This is the English gloss for L38's Ñaučhän-mata'lɪn⁶; the two share one printed row and were segmented as separate ALTO lines (L38 native term, L37 gloss) — kept as their own lines per the store, not merged.

41.text: Ñeumiˊrit (“woman umiˊrit”) Son-in-law’s or daughter-in-law’s mother.

42.text: ¹ Women use the term ñawˊgêl, which is the female pronunciation of ñaw-yêᵋˊlhɪ.
42.resolved: ¹=U+00B9 footnote marker; ñ=n+U+0303 (x2); ˊ=U+02CA (x2); ê=e+U+0302 (x2); ᵋ=U+1D4B; ɪ=U+026A
42.note: Advisory: rare form ñawˊgêl (keying_spec §5.1). Read directly off the raster (review/3-005/sheets/lines-42-48.png and zoom4-47p20-55_48p0-38.png context): stress tick clearly after w, before g, ê with circumflex — no dropped mark found, no g-dot expected here (this is not the -gɪn/-gin suffix, it is a bare root gêl).

43.text: ² Female pronunciation, ᴇʟuˊwg̣o-tɵˊmg̣ɪn. ᴇʟOO and ᴇʟuˊe are related.
43.note: "ELOO" is read literally off the raster (review/3-005/zoom/zoom4-43p0-49_43p27-76_44p0-35.png, row 43.1): two adjacent round letters at cap height, no apostrophe between them, where every other occurrence of this root on the page is ᴇʟo'o (stress, single o twice: L11, L12, L20). Possibly a compositor's contraction/cross-reference shorthand rather than the full form; flagging for adjudication rather than silently normalizing to ᴇʟo'o.

44.text: ³ Female pronunciation, ñauʟuˊwg̣o-tɵˊmg̣ɪn. Women among themselves use simply the term ñawˊgêl.
44.note: Same rare form ñawˊgêl as L42 (keying_spec §5.1 advisory); read the same way off the raster, no dropped mark found.

45.text: ⁴ For instance, uwäˊᵋqučilqäl (“intended for husband”), “bridegroom;” ñeˊwänlɪqäl (“intended for wife”), “bride.”
45.note: Stress precedes laryngeal here (uwäˊᵋ) where L4/L5/L6/L16/L42 print laryngeal before stress (êᵋˊ) — kept in the order printed rather than normalized to match, per the two-superscript-marks memory note.

46.text: ⁵ From the verb mataˊrkɪn (“thou takest,” “thou takest to wife”).

47.text: ⁶ Aaˊčêk means “young man;” ñeˊus˙qät means “woman.” These terms are used by both wedded parties.
47.note: Middle dot between s and q read as the palatalization mark U+02D9 (licensed on the seven-member series n x d t s č ǰ, and s is in that series), confirmed at 4x — not U+00B7 middle dot, which would be a lookalike per §3.

48.text: Sometimes they say also ᴇndêw-mataˊlɪn (“wife’s uncle”) and ᴇččaiˊñaw-mataˊlɪn (“wife’s aunt”).
